sourceContributions.qualification: New overlap mapping for the source's inflationary geometric-assumption and dynamics questions. Inherited assessments restrict it to generalized hyperinflation, distinguish side-tracked inflation and do not establish a classification of all rapid-turn models. Compatibility and reheating facets remain compound. Independent confirmation: u52 can specialize c0 through its geometric-assumption and inflationary-dynamics component. n31 and n84 restrict the assessment to generalized hyperinflation, distinguish side-tracked inflation and leave compatibility and reheating as separate compound facets.

New method contribution for metric-dependent multifield backgrounds and the geometric dependence of fluctuations. The supplied setting does not itself furnish a calculated spectrum or correlation result, and shift symmetry is not imposed universally. Independent confirmation: u68 supplies a metric-dependent multifield setting relevant as a method contribution to c0. n60 specifically limits the target to geometric dependence of fluctuations, while n59 prevents imposing shift symmetry. The role claims no calculated spectrum.

sources.title: Assisted inflation

evidence.text: An equal-field ansatz maps the identical-potential equations to a single canonical scalar through φ̃1² = mφ1², Ṽ = mV and p̃ = mp. For unequal slopes, a constant-ratio scaling ansatz and shifted, rescaled fields reduce all scalar equations consistently to one degree of freedom.

evidence.text: Integrates coupled background, two-point and three-point transport systems using a variable-step Runge–Kutta–Fehlberg integrator with error control. Field-space correlations are converted into curvature correlations using N_a and N_ab tensors.

sources.title: Partial UV Completion of $P(X)$ from a Curved Field Space

evidence.text: Numerically integrate the nonlinear planar PDEs and compare with the reduced single-field equations. The example uses P=X+X²/2, f=e^(2βχ), periodic boundaries, Δx=4×10⁻⁴ and Δt=2×10⁻⁴. The authors report cross-confirmation between independent C and Python/FEniCS implementations.

sources.title: Positivity vs. Lorentz-violation: an explicit example

evidence.text: Analyze quadratic spectra and Hamiltonians to identify stable heavy propagation modes. For the extended timelike EFT, use a canonical transformation and resum spatial derivatives; the argument chiefly uses two-point dynamics rather than four-point scattering.

sources.title: Consistency of EFT illuminated via relative entropy: a case study in scalar field theory

evidence.text: Write relative entropy in terms of Euclidean effective actions, integrate fields using tree-level saddle points, and expand in a bookkeeping parameter multiplying heavy–light interactions. General expressions are developed through cubic order; the two-field examples are evaluated through sixth order and compared with all-interaction-order tree-level results.

sources.title: The Effective Theory of Shift-Symmetric Cosmologies
